one_liner: Swift TOML 1.1 parser and Codable decoder. In its author's harness, its lazy parse ran about 5x faster than toml++.
what_it_does: A pure-Swift library for reading TOML (spec 1.1.0) with two API layers. `TOMLDecoder().decode(T.self, from:)` fills Decodable types; it has JSONDecoder-style key, date and time-interval strategies and lenient numeric and date conversions. `TOMLTable(source:)` returns a table with typed accessors such as `string(forKey:)`, `table(forKey:)` and `integer(atIndex:)` on `TOMLArray`. It only reads TOML: there is no encoder or writer, and it does not replace toml++ in C++ code.
how_it_is_fast: Parsing is two-phase: `TOMLTable(source:)` does a lexing-level pass that checks only structure (syntax, table redefinition, duplicate keys) and records each leaf value as a token byte range in five flat index-linked arrays instead of nested dictionaries, deferring unescaping and number/date validation to the typed accessor that asks for the value. The hot loop reads an UnsafeBufferPointer over the String's contiguous UTF-8 (avoiding String-index bounds checks) and scans basic strings 8 bytes at a time with a SWAR has-byte test for quote, backslash and newline. Key lookups are linear scans filtered by a cheap packed/sampled UInt64 key hash and a per-table 64-bit Bloom mask, with array capacities pre-reserved from input size. Per the author, most of the 0.4.3 micro-optimizations were found by an AI coding agent iterating on package-benchmark instruction counts.
when_to_use: Swift code on Apple platforms, Linux or Windows that loads TOML config into Codable types and wants a pure-Swift parser with no C/C++ dependency.
Large TOML documents (hundreds of KB, like the 443 KB twitter.toml fixture) where only some fields are read: untouched leaf values are tokenized but never validated or materialized.
Swift projects now calling tomlc99 or toml++ through C/C++ interop: the author measured 1.81x and 4.96x faster structural parses from Swift.
Code that wants strictly typed TOML access (Int64, Double, OffsetDateTime, LocalDate/LocalTime) and a choice of proleptic-Gregorian date conversion.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ programs: it is Swift-only, so toml++ or teptris stay the options there.
You need to write, edit or re-serialize TOML: it has no encoder, and `TOMLTable`'s Codable conformance throws `notReallyCodable` outside TOMLDecoder.

You need the whole document validated up front: `TOMLTable(source:)` accepts, for example, `x = foo` or a malformed date, and errors only when that value is read. Full checking needs `Dictionary(table)`, which the docs call expensive.

Untrusted or unusual input: the 0.4 rewrite is young. 0.4.5 (2026-07-11) fixed fuzzer-found traps such as `-=0` and wrongly rejected valid TOML 1.1 (`x = [[true]]`, `x = [[inf]]`). Tables with very many keys fall back to linear scans once the 64-bit Bloom mask saturates (inferred from source, not benchmarked).
Embedded Swift or Foundation-free builds: the module does `public import Foundation`. The trait to make it optional (issue #232, PR #316) is still open.

integration.form: module (SwiftPM package; also on the Bazel Central Registry as swift-tomldecoder)
integration.dependencies: Foundation only for the library target. The benchmark, swift-docc-plugin and SwiftFormat packages are pulled in only when env vars enable them.
integration.min_toolchain: Swift 6.0 (swift-tools-version 6.0; CI tests 6.0 and 6.3.3). Apple minimums are iOS 13, macOS 10.15, tvOS 13, watchOS 6 and visionOS 1.
integration.platforms: macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS (CI simulators), Ubuntu 24.04 and Windows 2025 in CI. WebAssembly is build-only (tests not run, issue #225). There is no architecture-specific code; the SWAR scan uses plain UInt64.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented in prose. TOMLTable, TOMLArray, TOMLDecoder and the date types are declared Sendable immutable structs, and the shared TOMLDocument is @unchecked Sendable with only `let` fields, so parsed results can be read concurrently. The parser is a per-call ~Copyable value.

gotchas: Errors come in two phases. A document can pass `TOMLTable(source:)` or start decoding and still throw later, from the accessor for a bad value. Only phase-1 errors are wrapped as `DecodingError.dataCorrupted` by `decode`.

Key strategies slow parsing: with `.convertFromSnakeCase` or `.custom`, every key is built as a String, transformed and rehashed during phase 1. The snake-case converter is marked `// TODO: make this fast`.

Possible trap with non-contiguous Strings, such as some bridged NSStrings. Parsing falls back to `withUTF8`, but TOMLDocument keeps the caller's original String, and the token accessors force-unwrap `utf8.withContiguousStorageIfAvailable`. This comes from reading TOMLDocument.swift and Token.swift and is not reported in issues. Passing a native String or Data avoids it.
Lookups by key (`string(forKey:)`, Codable containers) are linear scans of the table's entries, which the author chose deliberately. Cost per lookup grows with table width.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only Swift TOML entry in the catalog, so pick it for Swift code. For C/C++ pick teptris (C99; its own benchmarks show 5.2-8.5x toml++ throughput with a full DOM and an emitter), for Rust toml-spanner, and for Go go-toml v2.
verified_claims_summary: In the author's own Swift program (harness unpublished, snippets only; 2026-01-01 post released with 0.4.3), averaging 100 warm iterations on the 443,461-byte twitter.toml with CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent, TOMLDecoder's lazy `TOMLTable(source:)` took 1.232 ms vs 2.226 ms for tomlc99 `toml_parse` (1.81x) and 6.107 ms for toml++ `toml::parse` with exceptions via a C wrapper (4.96x). This compares a structure-only parse with toml++'s fully validated DOM, the wrapper's move-assign into a static table puts the previous DOM's teardown inside the timed window (our reading of the snippet), and no CPU, OS, compiler versions, flags or baseline versions are given.
status_note: Active, single-maintainer, MIT (108 stars): 0.4.5 (2026-07-11) fixed fuzzer-found crashes and 0.4.4 added TOML 1.1.0 plus another 24% cut in twitter.toml parse instructions, but the API is pre-1.0 and 0.4.1 broke source compatibility with 0.3.x.
